headline: OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said the company is entering a 'new era of discovery' after it published 372 new maths results made by an unreleased AI model.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a large claimed batch of maths results, but not all peer reviewed and the company's own claim.
importance_line: Mathematicians and researchers may soon face a flood of AI-made proofs to check, but the results come from OpenAI, a company with a stake, and not all have been peer reviewed.
summary: India Today reports that OpenAI released 372 maths results, on GitHub, produced by an unreleased AI model, and that Altman wrote on X, "We are entering a new era of discovery now." Many proofs were checked with the Lean proof-checking program, but not all have been peer reviewed, and an advisory group at the Institute for Advanced Study called the release "the beginning, not the completion" of understanding the work.
notes: CNBC TV18 page returned no text; read India Today (amp page) on the same story. India Today also says OpenAI solved the Navier-Stokes Millennium Challenge last month and that a New York University professor said the company may have used his work; those are India Today's statements and are not repeated as fact. Other outlets give different counts (722); India Today's 372 is used.
